body:
THE NARROWS BOARD — THREAD #7841
IS THE SIGNAL NETWORK RIGGED?
Original post by: dustwalker_c
Posted: cycle 14, week 6
Status: LOCKED (mod action, cycle 14 week 17)
Archived by: Pell-9 for community reference

---

[dustwalker_c | C-tier | 14 posts]
Going to get shouted down for this but I'll say it anyway.

I've been doing runs in the Gray Zone for three years. Courier work, two wetwork assists, a full extraction that went textbook. My broker, Masha at Cormorant, won't vouch me up because she says her reputation chain "doesn't reach the right ears" for B-tier recognition. She's the Gray Zone-side. The brokers who matter are Narrows-up. The people who would vouch for me are all C-tier same as me. So all our vouches just ping around inside the same dead-end network. I can do the work. I can't move.

Tell me that's not rigged.

---

[KROKAR | B-tier | 1,204 posts]
lol dustwalker you've been doing this for THREE YEARS and you're still C. maybe the network is telling you something. survival filter exists for a reason. if your whole vouching circle is C-tier maybe that's because the work you're doing is C-tier work.

---

[pale_meridian | B-tier | 387 posts]
KROKAR shut up for five seconds. dustwalker's point is legitimate and you know it.

The network IS structurally biased toward people who already have social capital. That's not a conspiracy, it's just how vouching works. You need someone with weight behind them to vouch for you. Weight comes from connections. Connections come from — guess what — already having connections. If you entered the market from a the Gray Zone community that doesn't have established broker relationships in the Narrows or above, you are running a fundamentally different race.

That doesn't mean the system is broken on purpose. But "not broken on purpose" and "fair" are not the same thing.

---

[KROKAR | B-tier | 1,204 posts]
oh so now we're doing sociology. great. very useful on a run.

---

[Threefold | unverified | 2 posts]
First post here but I broker out of the Narrows East corridor (not naming my house, you can guess why) and I want to give the practical answer to dustwalker's question because most people here are theorizing.

Here's how it actually works from my end:

When I aggregate reputation tokens, I'm not just counting drops, I'm tracing the chain. A vouch from someone I know personally or have worked with hits different than a vouch from a stranger. That's not bias, that's signal integrity. Anonymous vouches are worthless because they're trivially faked. So yes, your vouches have to come from people I trust, who trust you. That's the design.

The problem dustwalker is describing is real but it's not the network's fault. It's a resourcing problem. the Gray Zone-side brokers are operating with fewer connections to Narrows-up aggregators because Narrows-up aggregators don't take runs in the Gray Zone, so they never build those relationships. It's a gap in the infrastructure, not deliberate exclusion.

What I'd actually tell dustwalker: find one job — ONE — with a mixed crew that has Narrows-up members. Do good work. That's the bridge. It's slower than it should be. But it's there.

---

[dustwalker_c | C-tier | 14 posts]
@Threefold okay that's useful actually, thank you. But I want to push back on "not deliberate exclusion." I've been trying to get on mixed crews for two years. Narrows-up operators vet their crews through — you guessed it — their existing networks. Which I'm not in. The bridge you're describing has a door, and the door is locked from the inside.

---

[pale_meridian | B-tier | 387 posts]
Also want to raise something nobody's touching yet: Ghost tier.

I've heard it described as three different things in the last year. "Operators so dangerous they wiped their own records." "A rumor brokers invented to explain why certain jobs have no verifiable chain." And my personal favorite: "A classification that extremely well-connected people use to operate without accountability because their patrons have enough weight to make the network pretend they don't exist."

If the third one is true — and I think it probably is, at least some of the time — then Ghost tier isn't a feature of a decentralized system. It's the exact opposite. It's what happens when people with enough social capital can opt OUT of the system entirely while still benefiting from it.

---

[KROKAR | B-tier | 1,204 posts]
Ghost tier is ghost stories for freelancers who want to feel like there's something more interesting going on than the job. You're telling me some legendary operator is out there "erasing their records." From WHAT. The network is dead drops and vouch chains. You can't erase a dead drop. You can just stop leaving them.

---

[vantablk | A-tier | 891 posts]
Actually going to agree with KROKAR on the Ghost tier point, which feels bad.

The mystification of Ghost tier does real harm to working freelancers. It functions as a pressure release valve. "The system is unfair, but somewhere out there is a lone genius who escaped it entirely." That narrative keeps people chasing an impossible individual solution instead of asking structural questions. I've been at A for four years. I know the people in the rooms where these conversations happen. There is no secret tier of untouchables. There are just people with more connections and more money protecting those connections. That's it. That's the whole thing.

---

[pale_meridian | B-tier | 387 posts]
@vantablk but you're describing something that FUNCTIONS like a hidden tier even if nobody calls it that. "People with enough connections and money that the normal accountability mechanisms don't apply" — what's the operational difference?

---

[Threefold | unverified | 2 posts]
I'm going to share something I probably shouldn't.

I know of a specific case — not naming names, not giving enough detail to trace — where an operator's tier designation stayed at B for six years while they were doing work that was clearly A-weight by any honest measure. Not because their work wasn't good. Because the broker aggregating their region had a long-standing relationship with another operator who competed for the same jobs. The competing operator was A-tier. The broker's vouching decisions were shaped by that relationship.

The system is decentralized. That means there's no appeals process. No audit. If your broker is compromised — not even corrupt, just self-interested, which is the same thing in practice — you can wait out six years of underrating or you can find a new broker, which is its own kind of starting over.

I don't know what the solution is. I'm not sure there is one that doesn't recreate a centralized authority, and I've seen what centralized authorities do in this city. But I think people who say "the network is the best option we have" and people who say "the network replicates hierarchies" are both right and both missing something.

---

[hardline_m | C-tier | 66 posts]
Can I say something unpopular

This whole conversation is a distraction.

Whether the network is fair or unfair, rigged or just flawed, the city does not care. Arcturus does not care. the Gray Zone does not care about our tier designations. The water is still rising in the lower levels. The food contracts still exclude half the Gray Zone. People are taking any job they can get because the alternative is standing in a labor queue at a Tier 1 block-manager's discretion and hoping you get called.

We are arguing about whether our informal reputation system is meritocratic. Our informal reputation system exists because there is no other system. The question of whether it's fair is a real question but it is not the most important question. The most important question is what we do with what we have.

I don't know. I don't have the answer. I'm just tired of watching smart people spend energy on arguments that end with "the system has problems" like that's new information.

---

[dustwalker_c | C-tier | 14 posts]
@hardline_m I hear you. But naming the problem is still doing something. I don't have solutions either. I just wanted to say out loud that it's not pure meritocracy and stop feeling like the problem was me.

---

[vantablk | A-tier | 891 posts]
For what it's worth, dustwalker: it's probably not just you.
